episodes.210699: A cold front slowly dropping in from the north triggered scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms in an unseasonably warm airmass. A few of the storms produced gale-force wind gusts over the waters, both during the afternoon and with a second wave in the evening.
episodes.210700: A cold front slowly dropping in from the north triggered scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms in an unseasonably warm airmass. A few of the storms produced sporadic damaging wind gusts and large hail, both during the afternoon and with a second wave in the evening.
episodes.210701: A cold front slowly dropping in from the north triggered scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms in an unseasonably warm airmass. A few of the storms produced sporadic damaging wind gusts and large hail, both during the afternoon and with a second wave in the evening.
episodes.210739: At the surface, a cold front drifted southeastward across Lake Ontario, southern ON, and southern Lower MI toward Lake Erie during the early afternoon through late evening of the 31st. Ahead of the front, several lines of multicell thunderstorms and a discrete supercell persisted generally eastward across northern OH during the late afternoon through the late evening of the 31st. Some of these storms produced sporadic straight-line convective wind damage, two mesovortex-related tornadoes, and small hail. The ambient environment of these storms included weak to moderate MUCAPE and moderate to strong effective bulk shear. It appears the development of a southwesterly to west-southwesterly low-level jet and resulting enhanced surface-based ESRH coinciding with favorably-low mixed layer LCL's contributed to the development of the two tornadoes.
episodes.210797: A boundary set up across eastern Ohio and western Pennsylvania allowed for ample lift ahead of the cold frontal passage given sufficient instability and ample shear in place across the region during the afternoon and evening hours of March 31, 2026. These thunderstorms began to develop across western Ohio and gradually developed stronger as they continued tracking across central and eastern Ohio and into portions of western Pennsylvania. This line of thunderstorms along the boundary caused multiple instances of tree damage across Warren and McKean counties with no injuries reported despite all of the tree damage. A secondary surge of thunderstorms later in the evening allowed for a tree to get knocked down in Clearfield County, with no injuries reported from this incident.
episodes.210879: Scattered storms, mostly sub-severe, developed across northeast and east-central Kansas in the mid to late evening hours on March 31. One storm briefly produced hail around quarter size.
episodes.211057: A dryline emerged over the Rolling Plains on the afternoon of the 31st. At the same time, a cold front was moving southward which generated strong thunderstorms at the intersection of these two features. This activity initially formed over the southeastern Texas Panhandle and moved southward into the Rolling Plains during the evening hours. These storms produced a mix of large hail up to golf ball size along with severe wind gusts up to 68 mph.
episodes.211067: The first of April saw the third consecutive day of severe thunderstorms across the region. An upper level storm system moving out of the Rockies into the Central Plains brought moisture and lift over West Texas creating widespread rain showers and thunderstorms. Surface conditions across the caprock were relatively dry which led to numerous virga showers that brought severe wind gusts. Once this activity reached better moisture off the caprock, the showers developed into severe thunderstorms producing severe wind gusts. ||High wind gusts (non-thunderstorms) from Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet sites are listed below:||67 mph at New Deal (Lubbock County),|64 mph at Shallowater (Lubbock County),|62 mph at Reese Center (Lubbock County), |58 mph at Floydada (Floyd County), and|58 mph at Olton (Lamb County).||High wind reports (non-thunderstorms) from Automated Surface Observing Systems (ASOS) are listed below:||64 mph at Lubbock International Airport (Lubbock County).
episodes.211289: A dryline set up over central portions of the Permian Basin, extending southward towards the Big Bend. A nearby shortwave encouraged thunderstorm development east of this dryline. A couple of thunderstorms produced severe winds in the Permian Basin. Meanwhile, strong winds aloft coupled with the passage of a Pacific front allowed for high winds in the Guadalupe Mountains and in far northern portions of Lea County in SE New Mexico.
episodes.211293: Scattered to widespread showers and storms pressed through southeast Ohio on the first day of April ahead of a cold frontal passage. Strong to severe thunderstorms were first noted shortly after midday along the border of Kentucky and West Virginia, with more quickly infiltrating Ohio by peak heating hours. Storms grew strong enough to produce damaging wind gusts, 1 to 1.5 inch hail stones, and heavy downpours. Aside from numerous reports of large hail across Washington County, downed trees and power lines were observed, along with an isolated instance of flash flooding in Marietta. Storms pressed east of the Ohio River into West Virginia by the middle of the evening, bringing the severe weather threat to an end for southeast Ohio.
episodes.211295: Several rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms pressed through West Virginia on April 1st as a cold front progressed overhead. The first notable storm kicked things off shortly after midday in Wayne County, with large hail and damaging wind gusts that resulted in local power outages. Additional storm damage progressed through the state over the course of the afternoon and evening as more development occurred ahead of the frontal passage. In addition to the downed trees and power lines, heavy downpours accompanying storms in the Parkersburg area led to street flooding along several roads in the city. The loss of daytime heating brought the severe threat of storms to an end that evening.
episodes.211397: Ahead of a southeastward moving cold front, broken lines of showers and thunderstorms developed in the evening hours. A surge of mid 70s temperatures with upper 50s dew points resulted in sufficient destabilization with MLCAPE up to 1000 J/kg, effective shear of 30-40 knots, and a gradient of 700-900 DCAPE. This allowed for some thunderstorms to become severe with large hail and damaging wind as the result, including two measured 58 mph gusts in southwest Pennsylvania.
episodes.211605: Scattered storms moved across southern Kansas the evening and night of March 31. A couple of these storms became severe producing wind gusts up to 60 mph and hail up to half-dollar size.
episodes.211638: A quasi-stationary front drifted into northern Virginia, supported aloft by a weak upper level trough, provided instability for a few severe thunderstorms to develop. Lapse rates of around 6-7 degrees C/km and CAPE values between 1000-2000 J/kg were observed, in addition to afternoon surface temperatures in the 80s, triggered thunderstorms that produced large hail.
episodes.211639: A quasi-stationary front drifted into northern Virginia, supported aloft by a weak upper level trough, provided instability for a few severe thunderstorms to develop. episodes.211761: An intensifying upper storm system instigated a period of severe thunderstorms across much of the WFO Norman Forecast area during the evening of the 1st. Storm development occurred both along a quasi-stationary boundary across northern Oklahoma and along an accelerating Pacific Front from far western Oklahoma into western-north Texas. A mix of supercells and a well-developed quasi-linear convective system (QLCS) yielded reports of large to very large hail and wind damage across portions of the area.
episodes.211762: An intensifying upper storm system instigated a period of severe thunderstorms across much of the WFO Norman Forecast area during the evening of the 1st. Storm development occurred both along a quasi-stationary boundary across northern Oklahoma and along an accelerating Pacific Front from far western Oklahoma into western-north Texas. A mix of supercells and a well-developed quasi-linear convective system (QLCS) yielded reports of large to very large hail and wind damage across portions of the area. A brief tornado was also documented in far eastern Wilbarger County in Texas.
episodes.211984: A strong cold front opened up the month of April across northeast Kentucky, supplying a brief burst of strong to severe thunderstorms. The first storm of note passed through Lawrence County shortly after midday, leading to local power outages from downed trees and power lines. A few hours later, one more storm pressed through the county and prompted a single downed tree. The bulk of the convective activity then became focused in West Virginia, bringing the severe threat to northeast Kentucky to an end.
episodes.212014: A low pressure system impacted eastern New York on the final day of March of 2026, bringing widespread rainfall and evening thunderstorms as its associated cold front tracked through the region. Over the course of the event, a widespread 0.5 to 1.5 inches of rain fell across eastern New York with locally higher amounts up to nearly 2 inches in some spots. While most resulting thunderstorms were non-severe, one isolated severe storm developed late in the evening which downed multiple trees in Shandaken in Ulster County.
episodes.212047: A low pressure system impacted western Massachusetts on the final day of March of 2026, bringing widespread rainfall and evening thunderstorms as its associated cold front tracked through the region. Over the course of the event, about 0.5 to 1.3 inches of rain fell across western Massachusetts with the heaviest rainfall rates occurring within thunderstorms that tracked just ahead of the boundary in the late evening. While most thunderstorms proved to be sub-severe in strength, an isolated storm did, per radar estimation, produce a severe-level wind gust which downed a tree in Lenox.
episodes.212059: Warm and humid air to the south of a warm frontal boundary spawned heavy rain producing thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening. Storms repeatedly moving over the same regions produced pockets of 3 to 4 inches of rain which triggered areas of flash flooding.

episodes.212639: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon across the North Carolina  mountains and foothills. A couple of the storms produced hail.
episodes.212777: A wet pattern developed during the first days of the month as above normal moisture, a nearby upper-level trough and a weak  trade wind cap supported shower and thunderstorm development. This included frequent passing showers across windward sectors, followed by enhanced afternoon convection. Flooding and Landslide reports where received during this period, April 1st to 5th.
episodes.212822: A strong to severe thunderstorms produced isolated damaging winds.
episodes.212963: April 2026 was a wet month for much of Central NY (CNY), especially around the Finger Lakes region, as precipitation was 150%-200% of normal. Several reports of river flooding occurred during the first couple of days of the month due to heavy rainfall. Owasco and Onondaga Lakes also reported flooding early in the month, while Cayuga Lake at Ithaca was at or above flood stage for much of the month of April. Moderate and major flooding occurred on the inlet to Owasco Lake and along the Tioughnioga River.
episodes.213075: Scattered showers and storms developed ahead of a slow moving cold front on the evening of April 1, 2026.
episodes.213177: A complex storm system brought numerous severe thunderstorm winds to northern UT and a flash flooding event to the San Rafael Swell.
episodes.213193: A warm, moist, and unstable airmass was in place across southeast Louisiana on April 1st, with scattered afternoon thunderstorms developing as a weak disturbance approached. While wind shear was weak and storms remained poorly organized, a few stronger pulse-type storms briefly became severe. One storm over Washington Parish produced quarter-size hail in the Bogalusa area during the mid-afternoon.
episodes.213232: A mesoscale low with embedded thunderstorms tracked northeast across the Blue Mountain foothills, producing strong wind gusts across portions of Umatilla, OR and Walla Walla, WA counties the afternoon of the 1st.
episodes.213267: A severe thunderstorm moved across a portion of northeast Mississippi.

A very brief EF0 tornado with estimated peak winds of 85-mph impacted the Apple Creek area. The tornado began just west of Honeytown Road, impacted three residential properties as it moved eastward, and then ended just east of the road. The tornado uprooted and snapped trees, and caused some large tree branches to be impaled into the ground. A carport awning was lofted across a home and knocked over a TV antenna, which caused the chimney to collapse onto the roof. Additional impacts included a blown-down fence, roof damage, and damage to an external propane tank at other residences.
